blocks.s: 8. O soul, we have drawn out our talk a long while. For it was good for us to be here, contemplating with Peter and John the glory of the Bridegroom, and to remain long with him, if he willed that there be made here not two, not three tabernacles (Matthew 17:1-4), but one, in which we might be together and together take delight. But now the Bridegroom says: Let me go, for the dawn is already rising; you have already received the light of grace and the visitation you desired. So, having given his blessing, having deadened the sinew of the thigh and changed the name Jacob into Israel (Genesis 32:25-31), the Bridegroom, long desired, quickly slipping away, withdraws for a little. He withdraws himself both from the vision spoken of and from the sweetness of contemplation; yet he remains present as far as governing goes.
